description_summary: 12-month unduplicated student headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and race/ethnicity for undergraduate and graduate students. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV, and contains total headcounts for men and women plus counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories.

12-month instructional activity totals broken down by undergraduate versus graduate level and reported as credit hours and/or contact hours. The table is for institution-level activity during the period, with records organized by institution and instructional level.

Institution-level academic library data for fiscal year 2014, covering library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services. The survey applies only to degree-granting institutions; expenditure fields are available only for institutions reporting total expenditures over $100,000. The survey entered IPEDS in 2014-15, and no separate even/odd-year reporting rule is stated.

Fall 2014 undergraduate admissions data for entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students, including admission considerations, applicants, admitted applicants, admitted students who enrolled, and SAT/ACT test scores. The table applies only to institutions without an open-admissions policy for entering first-time students; test-score fields are available for institutions that require scores for admission.

Awards and degrees conferred by six-digit CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, with totals and male/female counts for each of the nine race/ethnicity categories.

Students receiving any degree or certificate, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. There is one record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID, containing total, male, and female student counts for each of the nine race/ethnicity categories.

Students receiving awards, broken down by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age category. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age groups are under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age are not available in combination.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education, broken down by CIP program and award level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE; six-digit CIP records show award-level offerings and distance-education offerings, two-digit CIP records summarize the six-digit programs within the group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL, with total, men’s, and women’s counts and full-time and part-time counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL, with total, men’s, and women’s counts across all nine race/ethnicity categories and full-time and part-time counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFDELEV and includes total enrollment, exclusive, some, and no distance-education enrollment; exclusive distance-education enrollment is further classified by location as the same state or jurisdiction, a different state or jurisdiction, the U.S. with unknown state or jurisdiction, or outside the U.S.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY; age enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2014 (even) has data only from institutions that chose to report it.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE; residence enrollment reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2014 (even) has data under the catalog’s rule that it is collected only when institutions report it in the applicable collection cycle.

Fall enrollment counts in selected major fields broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, major field, and EFCIPLEV; coverage is limited to four-year institutions and the listed fields: education, engineering, biological/life sciences, mathematics, physical sciences, business management and administrative services, law, dentistry, and medicine.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, keyed by UNITID. The measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students; only academic-year institutions report entering-class data, and institutions offering short programs of less than one year do not have retention data.
Institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards; each record is one institution identified by UNITID.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for all private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions that use FASB accounting standards; each record is one institution identified by UNITID.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for private for-profit institutions using FASB standards; each record is one institution identified by UNITID. In 2014, the for-profit form includes expanded revenue sources and expense-function fields comparable to the not-for-profit form.

Graduation outcomes through 200% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates. It covers bachelor’s degree-seeking cohorts from 2006 at four-year institutions and cohorts from 2010 at less-than-4-year institutions; the four-year records report bachelor’s completions, while the less-than-4-year records report completion of any degree or certificate.

Graduation outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. It covers four-year bachelor’s degree-seeking cohorts from 2008 and two-year cohorts from 2011, with completion and transfer outcomes through 150% of normal time; records are uniquely defined by UNITID and cohort/graduation status (GRTYPE). For two-year institutions, 100%-of-normal-time completions are not available by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation outcomes for the 2011 cohort of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment, completion within 100% or 150% of normal time, and transfer-out status.

Staff counts by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty and tenure status, and contract type for applicable occupations. Each institution can have multiple records, uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which defines the occupational category and tenure-status grouping.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by the combined faculty/tenure status and academic rank, plus race/ethnicity and gender; non-tenure-track staff also have contract-type classifications. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines FACSTAT and ARANK; race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2014 (even) has no data for all institutions.

Full-time new-hire counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender; instructional new hires additionally have faculty/tenure-status categories. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which defines the occupation and, for instructional staff, faculty/tenure status; Human Resources reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2014 (even) has no data for all institutions.

Fall payroll staff counts by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- or part-time status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, which combines occupational category with full-/part-time status; race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2014 (even) has no data for all institutions.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and, for staff not on a tenure track or in a no-tenure system, contract type. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, the faculty/tenure-status grouping.

Counts, salary outlays, and weighted average monthly salaries for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK, the academic rank.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical, noninstructional staff, broken down by occupational category.
Custom comparison-group membership for the 2015 IPEDS Data Feedback Report, identifying each reporting institution and its comparison institutions by unitid, institution name, and state.

Response and applicability status for each institution and survey component, with rows keyed by unitid and component. It identifies reported, nonreported or imputed, and not-applicable components, parent/child multi-campus reporting, and revised submissions in final or revised releases.

Directory information for each institution, with one row per institution identified by unitid. It includes name and location, institutional URLs, active and Title IV participation status, control and institutional level, highest award level and degree, and Carnegie classifications.

Institutional offerings and organization by unitid, including program and award levels offered, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, admissions information, services, and athletic associations.

Student charges for full academic-year programs, keyed by unitid and student/program category. It covers full-time and part-time undergraduate and graduate charges, professional-practice doctoral charges, and published first-time undergraduate cost-of-attendance components for institutions whose programs are primarily credit-hour based and use semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or another academic calendar.

Student charges by vocational or occupational program, keyed by unitid and program. It applies to institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, reporting the number of programs, charges and attendance costs for the largest program, plus tuition, fees, and books and supplies for up to five additional programs.
Mission statement information for each institution, keyed by unitid, containing either the institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is available.

Undergraduate student financial aid counts and dollar amounts broken down by student population and aid source/type. The rows distinguish full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from all undergraduates; aid categories include federal, Pell, state/local, institutional, and federal or nonfederal loans for the first group, and total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans for all undergraduates. Variables include the number of recipients and total and average aid amounts, with institution and student-population/aid-category defining the record grain.

Average net price and the underlying grant, scholarship, and Title IV aid amounts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, reported separately for students receiving any grant or scholarship aid and students receiving Title IV federal aid. The table includes the 2011-12, 2012-13, and 2013-14 reporting years; for public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying in-district or in-state tuition. Institution, reporting year, and aid-recipient group define the record grain.

Military, servicemember, and veteran benefit recipients and benefit dollars broken down by benefit program and student level. The benefit categories are Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits and the Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program, and the populations include both undergraduate and graduate students; institution, student level, and benefit type define the record grain.
